intro: When the plain agent loop isn't enough — when steps branch, when you need to backtrack, when wall-clock matters — you reach for an explicit planning strategy. Four common ones, each with a different cost / robustness tradeoff. None is universally better; the right one depends on task shape.

items.title: ReAct (Reason + Act)
items.whenToUse: Default for tool-using agents. Tasks where each step is small and verifiable.
items.mechanism: Interleaved thought / action / observation. Model writes its rationale, picks a tool, sees the result, updates rationale, repeats. The 'plain agent loop' from Module F is ReAct.
items.tradeoff: Simple, debuggable, low overhead. Fails on long horizons because reasoning is greedy — no global plan.

items.title: Plan-and-Execute
items.whenToUse: Task decomposes cleanly. Sub-tasks are independent or have clear dependencies.
items.mechanism: Planner LLM emits a structured plan up front (list of sub-tasks, dependencies). Executor runs each in order or in parallel. Re-plan only if a sub-task fails.
items.tradeoff: Better wall-clock when sub-tasks parallelize. Brittle if the task discovery is dynamic — early plan goes stale fast.

items.title: Reflexion
items.whenToUse: Task has a verifiable success signal (tests pass, output matches schema, judge approves).
items.mechanism: Run, evaluate, reflect (write a self-critique), retry with the critique in context. Bounded by max-retries.
items.tradeoff: Climbs quality measurably. Cost is N× a single attempt. Stops cleanly when the signal is binary; fuzzy when it isn't.

items.title: Tree-of-Thoughts
items.whenToUse: Search problems where exploring multiple paths is genuinely useful (proofs, puzzles, plan-search).
items.mechanism: At each node, expand K candidate next-steps; score each (via the same or a judge model); keep top-M; recurse to depth D. Beam search over reasoning chains.
items.tradeoff: K × M × D blowup in cost and latency. Justified on a narrow class of problems; almost never the answer for chat or code agents.

items.title: Self-Ask
items.whenToUse: Multi-hop factual questions where decomposition into sub-questions is natural.
items.mechanism: Model writes 'Follow-up question:', answers it (often via a tool), then writes the next follow-up. Stops when no more follow-ups are needed.
items.tradeoff: Cleanest pattern for QA-over-knowledge. Underpowered for open-ended tasks.

pitfalls.title: Premature Tree-of-Thoughts
pitfalls.body: Engineers reach for ToT because it sounds smart. The cost is brutal and 95% of tasks don't benefit. Try ReAct first; only escalate when you can demonstrate a measurable quality lift.

pitfalls.title: Stale plan with no re-planning
pitfalls.body: Plan-and-Execute on a dynamic task: the plan is written before any real-world signal arrives, then executed past the point it stops being valid. Add a 're-plan' branch on failure.

pitfalls.title: Reflexion with a soft signal
pitfalls.body: If the success signal is 'an LLM judge thinks it's better', the loop drifts. Make signals binary (tests pass / schema matches) before you reach for Reflexion.

pitfalls.title: No budget
pitfalls.body: Every planning strategy explodes cost. Set a hard token + dollar + wall-clock budget per task, and cancel cleanly when hit. Don't 'just one more iteration'.

pitfalls.title: Comparing to baseline alone
pitfalls.body: Reporting 'Reflexion +12% over single-shot' hides whether vanilla ReAct already got +10% for 1/10th the cost. Always include the cheap baseline.

<!-- Planning-strategy decision fragment for an agent's system prompt -->

Before picking a strategy, answer these questions:

1. Is each step small and verifiable? → ReAct.
2. Does the task decompose into independent sub-tasks discoverable up front? → Plan-and-Execute.
3. Is success a binary signal (test, schema, exact match)? → Reflexion on top of ReAct.
4. Is this a search problem with branching where most paths are dead ends? → Tree-of-Thoughts.
5. Is this a multi-hop factual question? → Self-Ask.

If two strategies seem to apply, pick the cheaper one and only escalate if it fails. Track per-strategy: token cost, wall-clock, success rate. Re-evaluate weekly.
